topic: M4 Pro vs M5 Pro MacBook local LLM inference: MoEShift 374 tok/s prefill
title: 374 tok/s Prefill on M5 Pro: A First-Word Upgrade
description: MoEShift's author benchmarked the same 125B MoE model on 24 GB M4 Pro and M5 Pro MacBooks: prefill ran 199 versus 374 tok/s, while decode reached only 13.14 tok/s.
hook_candidates: M4 Pro or M5 Pro? One number decides.
Three hundred seventy four tokens a second, and not one is the answer.
Your Mac reads the prompt fast. Writing the answer is the slow part.
A 125 billion parameter model on a 24 GB Mac, at 8.5 GB of RAM.
Same model, same quant, same memory. Double the speed.
The new MacBook's SSD just doubled your prefill.
199 versus 374. The chip didn't get twice as fast.
You paste a long document. The cursor blinks. That's prefill.
The wait before the first word is the benchmark nobody runs.
Faster storage, not a faster GPU, moved this number.
narration_full: Three hundred seventy four tokens a second. None of them is the answer. Prefill reads your whole prompt before answering. You know that blinking cursor; everyone says only the newest chip fixes it. MoEShift's author ran both chips himself, same model, same quant. M four Pro prefill: one hundred ninety nine tokens a second. His explanation: not the GPU, not even memory bandwidth, but a faster SSD streaming in the experts each token needs. Decode, the actual writing, only reaches thirteen point one four tokens a second. A first-word upgrade, not a chat-speed upgrade.
